what_its_for: Erenumab-aooe is used to help prevent migraine headaches in adults. It works by blocking a protein in your body called CGRP, which plays a big role in causing migraines. Taking this medicine regularly can reduce how often you get migraines.
how_to_take: This medicine comes as a liquid in a prefilled autoinjector pen or prefilled syringe that you inject under your skin (subcutaneous injection). You will inject it into your stomach, thigh, or upper arm. Before your first dose, your doctor or nurse will show you exactly how to use it. Always let the pen or syringe warm up at room temperature for at least 30 minutes before injecting. Do not shake it. Clean the injection site with an alcohol swab, let it dry, then inject. Rotate your injection sites each time so you do not always inject in the same spot.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 70 mg injected once a month. Your doctor may increase your dose to 140 mg once a month (given as two separate 70 mg injections back to back) if needed. Always follow your doctor's instructions about your specific dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, give yourself the injection as soon as you remember. Then schedule your next dose one month from that date. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store your autoinjector pens or prefilled syringes in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do NOT freeze them. Keep them in the original carton to protect them from light. If needed, you may store them at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 7 days. Once kept at room temperature, do not put them back in the refrigerator. Throw away any pen or syringe left at room temperature for more than 7 days. Keep out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: There are no specific foods, drinks, or activities you must strictly avoid while taking this medicine. However, talk to your doctor before starting any new prescription or over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements, as they could interact with your treatment. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, let your doctor know before using this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: serious allergic reaction signs such as swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat; trouble breathing or swallowing; a severe rash or hives; dizziness or lightheadedness. Also call your doctor if you have constipation that is severe or does not go away, or if you notice any unusual pain, redness, swelling, or skin changes at the injection site that do not improve.
when_it_works: Most people start to notice fewer migraines within the first month of treatment. Some people may need up to 3 months to see the full benefit. Keep using it as directed even if you do not notice immediate improvement. Do not stop using it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before using this medicine, as it is not fully known how it may affect an unborn baby or nursing infant. This medicine is not approved for use in children or teenagers. Older adults can generally use this medicine safely, but should discuss any concerns with their doctor.
